projects.title: Fantasy Football Predictor
projects.question: Can a player's recent form and next opponent predict his fantasy points next week?
projects.finding: Yes, modestly. The model beats the naive recent-average baseline in every test season, mainly by pulling hot and cold streaks back toward normal. The next-opponent matchup feature added almost nothing.

data.note: Walk-forward test: trained on earlier seasons, tested on 2022 and 2023. Matchup feature changed R² by +0.001.

projects.title: Why Kickers Are Unpredictable
projects.question: Is a kicker's weekly fantasy score predictable, and if not, why?
projects.finding: Good offenses trade field goals for touchdowns. Betting lines predict extra-point volume well, but field goal volume, which drives almost all kicker variance, has no link to anything known before kickoff.

data.note: 2021–2024 regular seasons, 1,971 kicker-weeks. Walk-forward R² by season.

projects.title: Champions League Clash of Styles
projects.question: When Europe's top leagues meet, do some playing styles beat others?
projects.finding: It's a ladder, not rock-paper-scissors. The higher a team sits on the possession and control scale, the better it does, about 0.82 goals per step (R² 0.158, p < 0.0001). Style is tangled up with squad quality, so this is a signal, not proof of cause.

data.note: 127 Big-5 vs Big-5 matches, 2022–23 and 2024–25. Style gap = home style rank minus away style rank.

projects.title: March Madness and the Transfer Portal
projects.question: Does roster continuity predict tournament upsets in the transfer-portal era?
projects.finding: Not beyond seeding: adding continuity moved upset prediction from 0.705 to 0.708 AUC. But year-to-year team quality has become clearly more volatile since the portal opened.

data.note: 620 NCAA tournament games. Volatility = standard deviation of year-over-year change in adjusted net rating.
